exec: // Remember how many products exist, to prove the injection did not change or leak anything.
pm.test('product count unchanged after injection attempt', () => pm.expect(res.json().length).to.eql(Number(pm.environment.get('productCountBefore'))));

item.name: Login: SQL injection in email (rejected by validation)
Login: SQL injection that passes email validation
Register: SQL injection in name is stored safely

exec: pm.test('name stored exactly as sent', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().name).to.eql("'; DROP TABLE users;--"));
// Users table must still exist: the admin can still log in.
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ email: pm.environment.get('adminEmail'), password: pm.environment.get('adminPassword') }) },
}, (err, res) => pm.test('users table still intact (admin can log in)', () => pm.expect(res.code).to.eql(200)));
